text:
Raj: sketching a per-tenant degrade + fallback model for canary/A-B rollouts. idea: make fallback decisions token-budget aware and tenant-scoped rather than global.

Anna: +1. can you sketch sequence? is this reactive (on error) or proactive (budget met)?

Raj: both. two axes: failure-triggered (errors/timeouts) and budget-triggered (token or cost burn rate). policy decides ordered fallbacks: 1) quantized variant on same infra, 2) smaller architecture (faster but lower quality), 3) cached/prefix response, 4) degrade to summary-only API.

Kevin: curious about latency implications. switching to quantized might add switching cost. do we warm KV cache for quantized variants?

Raj: yes — warm plan: maintain lightweight affinity (session -> variant) and a tiny async warmup for variants likely to receive traffic. if budget warning hits, we pre-queue warmups.

Sara: what about hedging vs sync fallback? My vote: try a single fast hedge (race to quantized) for high-p50 routes, otherwise synchronous fallback to avoid token waste.

Raj: agreed. propose a routing rule: if p50 < 200ms and request_length < 256 -> hedged race to quantized (10ms hedging window). else synchronous fallback.

Jen: telemetry contract? ops needs signals to auto-unwind fallback once health/budget improves.

Raj: minimal telemetry: per-tenant
- fallback_active (bool)
- tokens_saved_last_min (int)
- quality_regression_delta (float)
- fallback_reason_tags (list)
these must be emitted at 1s granularity to our metrics bus.

Kevin: nice. also add "fallback_entropy" so we can detect oscillation (back-and-forth).

Raj: good call. add circuit-stability score.

OpsBot: deploy check: rollout UI needs to show per-tenant budget usage and live simulation of degrade path.

Anna: config snippet would help product + console folks.

Raj: paste proto-like sketch:
rollout_policy: {
  mode: "token-budgeted-canary"
  tenants: [
    {id: "tenant:alpha", max_extra_tokens_per_min: 5000, fallback_chain: ["model-q8-v2","model-small-v1","cached-summary"]},
    {id: "tenant:beta", max_extra_tokens_per_min: 200, fallback_chain: ["model-q8-v2","cached-summary"]}
  ]
  hedging_window_ms: 10
  stability_quorum_ms: 60000
}

Sara: good. what about ownership? who owns per-tenant budgets? billing? product?

Raj: operationally owned by platform; budget thresholds sourced from billing/tenant plan. product can request overrides for experiments. need an audit log.

Kevin: edge case: multi-variant session fidelity. if we fallback mid-response to different model semantics might change tokens produced and break callers. we should only allow variant that preserves function contract or run a lightweight normalization layer.

Jen: add safety: accept-only-compat variants + a transform layer that enforces response schema (e.g., JSON schema + tokenized prefix checks).

Raj: decision points for RFC:
- telemetry fields & rate (1s vs 10s)
- hedging window per-route vs global
- warming strategy and memory budget for affinities
- ownership mapping to billing/product
- UI simulator contract

Anna: can you turn this into an RFC stub? i can prep the ops/console requirements.

Raj: will do. pinging @Kevin @Sara @Jen for reviews. :slightly_smiling_face:

Kevin: LGTM, small nit: make hedging_window configurable per-model-size.

Sara: +1

OpsBot: created RFC draft #rfc-arch-1765 in docs — assign reviewers Raj, Anna, Kevin, Sara, Jen.
